intro.title: What are Garnet Gems?
intro.description1: Garnets are a group of silicate minerals that have been prized as gemstones since the Bronze Age. Renowned for their incredible brilliance and rich depth of color, garnets are most famous for their fiery red hues, though they occur in a vibrant spectrum of colors including deep oranges, greens, and warm purples.
intro.description2: Unlike many other gemstones, natural garnets are rarely treated with heat or chemicals, making them one of the most pure and authentic gemstone choices. With a Mohs hardness of 6.5 to 7.5, they possess exceptional durability, making them perfect for both heritage jewelry and modern designs.

reason1.title: 100% Ethical Sourcing
reason1.desc: Every single garnet is mined under strict ethical standards, respecting both the environment and our local mining communities.

reason2.title: Own Heritage Mines
reason2.desc: We eliminate middlemen entirely. By owning and operating our mines, we guarantee the exact origin and uncompromised quality of each gem.

reason3.title: Surgical Precision Cut
reason3.desc: Our master lapidarists craft custom facets tailored to each raw crystal, maximizing its fire, refraction, and optical depth.

reason4.title: International Certification
reason4.desc: Every gemstone is authenticated and graded by leading global laboratories (GIA, GIC, GRS), ensuring your investment is secure.

process.title: How We Process Our Garnets
process.description: Our vertical integration ensures the highest standard of quality control at every stage of the gemstone's journey, from the depths of the earth to a polished work of art.

step1.title: Ethical Extraction
step1.desc: We extract raw garnets from our private mines in Elahera and Ratnapura. Our sustainable mining techniques protect the local ecosystem and ensure safety.

step2.title: Expert Grading
step2.desc: Raw specimens are carefully evaluated by our geologists. Only stones with optimal saturation, clarity, and crystallization potential are selected.

step3.title: Artisanal Faceting
step3.desc: In our Colombo workshops, master cutters map each stone to determine the ideal shape (cushion, oval, round) that will unlock its inner fire.

step4.title: Proprietary Polish
step4.desc: We apply dynamic polishing techniques using fine diamond powder. This creates a highly reflective surface, giving the garnet its signature mirror-like luster.

step5.title: Certification & Export
step5.desc: Each finished garnet undergoes rigorous testing, is certified, and is packed in premium secure transit cases for export worldwide.

cta.title: Acquire a Piece of Eternity
cta.subtitle: Browse our handpicked inventory of certified natural garnets or collaborate with our designers for a bespoke creation.

hessonite.title: Hessonite Garnet
hessonite.subtitle: The Golden Cinnamon Stone
hessonite.desc: Known as the 'Cinnamon Stone', Hessonite Garnet displays a captivating golden-orange to honey-brown color with a distinctive internal glow. Unlike most garnets, its warm appearance is caused by unique crystal inclusions that create a soft, syrup-like effect.
hessonite.story: Historically revered in Vedic astrology as the gemstone of Rahu, the Hessonite Garnet has long been associated with wisdom, prosperity, and protection. Ancient Sri Lankan royalty and Indian nobility admired its glowing amber appearance, often incorporating it into ceremonial jewelry and royal ornaments.
hessonite.origin: Premium Hessonite Garnets are primarily mined in Sri Lanka, especially the gem-rich regions of Ratnapura and Elahera. Sri Lankan specimens are internationally renowned for their exceptional transparency and vibrant cinnamon-orange color.
hessonite.color: Golden Orange • Honey Brown • Cinnamon Red • Amber Orange
hessonite.clarity: Typically eye-clean with characteristic 'heat-wave' inclusions unique to natural Hessonite.
hessonite.rarity: High-quality transparent Hessonite with vivid orange color is relatively rare and highly valued.
hessonite.bestFor: Collectors, astrology enthusiasts, heritage jewelry, and unique statement pieces.

rhodolite.title: Rhodolite Garnet
rhodolite.subtitle: The Rose of the Garnet Family
rhodolite.desc: Rhodolite Garnet is a naturally occurring blend of Pyrope and Almandine Garnets. Its remarkable raspberry-red to purplish-pink color offers exceptional brilliance and a softer elegance than traditional deep-red garnets.
rhodolite.story: Named after the Greek word 'Rhodon', meaning rose, Rhodolite was first identified in North Carolina during the late nineteenth century. Today it is celebrated by jewelry designers for its vivid color, outstanding brilliance, and timeless sophistication.
rhodolite.origin: Sri Lanka produces exceptionally clean Rhodolite Garnets alongside deposits found in Tanzania, Mozambique, India, and Madagascar.
rhodolite.color: Rose Red • Raspberry • Purplish Red • Pinkish Violet
rhodolite.clarity: Usually eye-clean with excellent transparency and high brilliance.
rhodolite.rarity: Fine raspberry-colored Rhodolites with excellent clarity are considerably rarer than standard red garnets.
rhodolite.bestFor: Modern luxury jewelry, engagement rings, anniversary gifts, and premium gemstone collections.

pyrope.title: Pyrope Garnet
pyrope.subtitle: The Fire-Eyed Garnet
pyrope.desc: Pyrope Garnet is celebrated for its intense crimson to blood-red color and extraordinary brilliance. Rich in magnesium, it possesses remarkable transparency and often appears free from visible inclusions, making it one of the finest red garnets.
pyrope.story: The name 'Pyrope' comes from the Greek word meaning 'fire-eyed'. During the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries, Pyrope Garnets from Bohemia became famous throughout Europe and adorned royal crowns, military insignia, and aristocratic jewelry collections.
pyrope.origin: Pyrope Garnets are found in Sri Lanka, the Czech Republic, South Africa, Tanzania, and Mozambique.
pyrope.color: Deep Crimson • Blood Red • Scarlet Red • Dark Ruby Red
pyrope.clarity: Excellent transparency with very few natural inclusions.
pyrope.rarity: Fine blood-red Pyrope with superior saturation is increasingly rare and highly collectible.
pyrope.bestFor: Classic fine jewelry, heirloom collections, and timeless investment pieces.

almandine.title: Almandine Garnet
almandine.subtitle: The Timeless Deep Red Garnet
almandine.desc: Almandine Garnet is the most abundant member of the garnet family, admired for its rich burgundy-red to violet-red color. Premium-quality stones exhibit remarkable clarity, durability, and exceptional brilliance suitable for everyday luxury jewelry.
almandine.story: For thousands of years, Almandine Garnets have symbolized protection, strength, and loyalty. Ancient warriors believed these gemstones guarded them during battle, while medieval nobility treasured them as symbols of power, courage, and everlasting devotion.
almandine.origin: Sri Lanka produces exceptional gem-quality Almandine Garnets alongside deposits found in India, Brazil, Madagascar, and the United States.
almandine.color: Deep Red • Burgundy • Violet Red • Wine Red
almandine.clarity: High-quality stones are transparent with excellent durability and minimal inclusions.
almandine.rarity: Although Almandine is common, large, eye-clean, intensely colored gemstone-quality specimens are rare.
almandine.bestFor: Everyday fine jewelry, heirloom designs, wedding collections, and long-term gemstone investments.
